quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: In Hungary, September 14th is traditionally when people start harvesting grapes for wine-making season. The country has been producing wine for over 2,000 years, with Tokaji wine being one of the world's oldest sweet wines, dating back to the 1500s.

short_read.title: The Secret Lives of Banana Slugs
short_read.teaser: These bright yellow mollusks are the Pacific Northwest's gentle forest gardeners. Learn why they're so important to the Olympic Peninsula's ecosystem and why they can grow up to 10 inches long!

medium_read.title: The Fascinating History of the Strait of Juan de Fuca
medium_read.teaser: Named after a Greek sailor who may have never actually sailed it, this waterway connects Port Angeles to the Pacific. Its discovery story involves international intrigue, competing explorers, and indigenous peoples who knew it all along.

long_read.title: Olympic National Park: Three Ecosystems in One
long_read.teaser: From temperate rainforests to alpine peaks to rugged coastlines, discover how one park contains such remarkable diversity. This beautiful exploration takes you through the unique plants and animals that make each ecosystem special.

port_angeles.title: Black-Tailed Deer Season
port_angeles.description: September is when you might see more Columbian black-tailed deer near Park View Villas, as they move to lower elevations for fall. These gentle creatures are unique to the Pacific Northwest and are smaller than their white-tailed cousins. Keep an eye out during your morning walks!

puzzle_1.question: A banana slug can be up to ___ inches long, making it one of the largest slugs in North America.
puzzle_1.correct_response: That's exactly right, Barbara! These gentle giants can reach 10 inches — about as long as a pencil!
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! These amazing mollusks can reach up to 10 inches long.
puzzle_1.wrong_response: These remarkable creatures can actually grow up to 10 inches long — that's nearly a foot! They're the second-largest terrestrial slug in the world.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: Banana slugs are decomposers that help recycle nutrients in the forest. They're bright yellow to warn predators that they taste terrible!
puzzle_1.learn_more_label: More about banana slugs — National Park Service

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'hello' or 'goodbye'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Szia! You got it right, Ildiko! It's one of the most versatile and friendly words in Hungarian.
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The answer is 'Szia' (pronounced SEE-ah) — it's a warm, informal way to say both hello and goodbye to friends and family!
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Szia comes from the word 'szolga' meaning servant, originally part of the phrase 'your humble servant.' The more formal version is 'Sziasztok' when greeting multiple people.

puzzle_3.question: What is the Olympic Peninsula's temperate rainforest known for receiving each year?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Wonderful! The Hoh Rainforest gets over 140 inches of rain annually — that's nearly 12 feet! This creates those magical misty forests with hanging moss that make our area so special.
puzzle_3.wrong_response: Actually, the Olympic rainforests receive over 140 inches of rain each year — that's what makes them so lush and green! The Hoh Rainforest is one of the wettest places in the continental United States.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: All that rain creates perfect conditions for Sitka spruce and western hemlock trees to grow over 200 feet tall, and for moss and ferns to drape every surface in green.
puzzle_3.learn_more_label: About temperate rainforests — Olympic National Park
